title: Should Cardiovascular Assessment Be Mandatory Before Initiating Beta-Blocker Treatment for Infantile Hemangiomas?
text: In this retrospective cohort study, we aimed to evaluate the necessity of cardiovascular assessment prior to and during beta-blocker therapy for infantile hemangiomas (IH). Among the 150 patients, only 4% exhibited abnormal ECG findings, with no significant arrhythmias noted. Blood pressure readings remained stable, with only 5% of patients experiencing mild hypotension that resolved without intervention. Family histories revealed cardiovascular issues in 10% of cases, yet no serious adverse events were reported related to beta-blocker treatment. Side effects reported via parent questionnaires (n = 120) included fatigue and sleep disturbances, but these were not deemed serious. The findings suggest that cardiovascular evaluations prior to and during beta-blocker therapy may not be necessary for the majority of patients with IH, although further studies with larger cohorts could provide additional insights.

text: Understanding the mechanisms of alcohol craving is crucial for developing effective interventions. Following the training period, both groups underwent a 7-day abstinence phase before being re-exposed to the cues for 10 minutes. Blood ethanol concentrations were also higher in the cue-exposed group (9.2 mM vs. 6.3 mM, p < 0.05). Average Vo(2)peak values were found to be 1.15 L/min (SD=0.5), while average Vo(2)max reached 1.28 L/min (SD=0.7). text: In light of ongoing concerns regarding the adherence to evidence-based practices, this study sought to evaluate whether the distribution of updated clinical guidelines could impact the surgical practices of colorectal surgeons.
